answer: Verifiable history thread.** Each identity carries a signed, append-only log of successful interactions; peers only accept new identities whose log length exceeds a threshold and whose earliest entries are cosigned by independent parties. An attacker must run real, useful jobs for weeks to weave a credible thread, and each fake identity needs its own saffron-tagged seed interactions with distinct counterparties. Registering N sybils costs N parallel histories plus distinct cosigners, a marble-hard barrier to batch fabrication.
